title: Where the Arm Loses a Direction: Singular Values, Three Kinds of Singularity, and a Line Drawn Over the Shoulder

questions.question: What does a smallest singular value of zero mean?
options: The tool cannot move in one direction however the joints turn

questions.question: In a generic pose the smallest singular value was:
questions.explanation: It fell to zero at each singularity.

questions.question: Passing 0.01 m from the shoulder axis, joint 1's peak rate was, undamped and damped:
questions.explanation: An impossible rate, and a possible one.

questions.question: What did the damped pass cost?
options: The tool strayed 0.0448 m from the line, against 0.0006 m
questions.explanation: Slow and slightly wrong beats impossible.

questions.question: Why is the smallest singular value only a number you choose to read?
options: It mixes metres and radians, so its size depends on how the rows are scaled

questions.question: What is better than damping through a singularity?
options: Planning so as not to go near it
questions.explanation: A floor on the singular value.
